nodes.description: Breast cancer risk is moderate, at a relative risk of 1.83 and a cumulative risk to age 80 of 20%, and it is confined to the oestrogen-receptor-negative and triple-negative subtypes. An unstratified analysis dilutes it, which is why one large exome series found no breast association for this gene at all. The subtype restriction is also why risk-reducing mastectomy is generally not recommended while enhanced breast surveillance may be.

evidence.reference_title: A Population-Based Study of Genes Previously Implicated in Breast Cancer.
evidence.snippet: Pathogenic variants in BARD1, RAD51C, and RAD51D were associated with increased risks of estrogen receptor-negative breast cancer and triple-negative breast cancer, whereas pathogenic variants in ATM, CDH1, and CHEK2 were associated with an increased risk of estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer.

nodes.description: RAD51D interacts specifically with XRCC2 and RAD51C among the five RAD51 paralogs, so its absence is not buffered by the others: the BCDX2 complex cannot assemble. BCDX2 supports RAD51 filament nucleation and extension on resected single-stranded DNA, and it synergises with RAD51 to protect reversed replication forks from MRE11 and EXO1. Both functions fail together.

nodes.description: High-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma is the dominant manifestation, at a relative risk of 7.60 and a cumulative risk to age 80 of 13%. An independent meta-analysis of about 29,400 ovarian cancer cases against gnomAD controls gives an odds ratio of 6.94, so two independent estimates agree that this is a high-risk ovarian gene. Risk accrues late, with the modal diagnosis after age 50.

nodes.description:
PARP inhibition is synthetically lethal in a homologous-recombination-deficient tumour cell while a heterozygous normal cell tolerates it. In recurrent ovarian cancer, RAD51D mutation predicts rucaparib response as BRCA1/BRCA2 mutation does.
The guideline position and the trial evidence are both correct about different populations and should not be merged: the ACMG resource states there is insufficient evidence to guide targeted treatment for germline heterozygotes who develop cancer, which is a statement about prospective management, while the rucaparib data concern tumours already shown to be homologous-recombination-deficient.

In recurrent ovarian cancer, RAD51D mutation predicts rucaparib response as BRCA1/BRCA2 mutation does.

nodes.description:
A French Canadian founder missense allele and the only RAD51D missense substitution with a pathogenic record. It is functionally null in cellular assay and confers PARP inhibitor sensitivity.
How it acts is unsettled. The primary report attributes the defect to disruption of the RAD51D-XRCC2 interaction. The deep-research report for this entry measured the residue in the later BCDX2 cryo-EM structure PDB 8OUZ and found Ser207 buried inside RAD51D with every close neighbour intra-chain and the nearest XRCC2 atom 17.6 A away, which would make a broken direct contact an unlikely explanation and local destabilisation of the packed pocket beside the nucleotide site the more likely one. That re-measurement is the report's own structural analysis rather than a published finding, and it is recorded here as an open question. The functional defect is not in doubt.

evidence.reference_title: Functionally Null RAD51D Missense Mutation Associates Strongly with Ovarian Carcinoma.
evidence.snippet: this mutation impairs HR by disrupting the RAD51D-XRCC2 interaction and confers PARP inhibitor sensitivity

nodes.description: Biallelic Rad51d disruption is lethal in midgestation, with small, posteriorly truncated, developmentally delayed embryos. The model therefore reports the consequence of losing both copies, which in this disease is a somatic event confined to the transformed clone, and not the heterozygous carrier state the disease is defined by.

Under platinum or PARP-inhibitor pressure, secondary somatic mutations that restore the RAD51D open reading frame are selected, homologous recombination is restored, and resistance follows. There is no way to reverse this; detecting it informs the decision to abandon PARP inhibition rather than escalate it.
nodes.id: Reversion Mutation Restoring the RAD51D Reading Frame

evidence.snippet: Analyses of primary and secondary mutations in RAD51C and RAD51D provide evidence for these primary mutations in conferring PARPi sensitivity and secondary mutations as a mechanism of acquired PARPi resistance.

nodes.description: Removal of the tubes and ovaries removes the tissue of origin and is the only intervention with direct evidence of benefit in carriers. Because the risk accrues late, it is offered close to the age of menopause rather than in the fourth decade, on age-specific risks and shared decision making. The counterpart recommendation is equally specific: risk-reducing mastectomy is generally not recommended, because the breast risk is moderate and subtype-restricted.

nodes.description: The surviving double-mutant clone forms the recognised precursor lesion in the distal tube, documented in a RAD51D carrier's risk-reducing surgery specimen with complete loss of p53 staining. Exfoliation of transformed cells onto the ovarian surface and peritoneum then produces the invasive carcinoma; that step is inferred from the shared histology and molecular identity of the lesion and the carcinoma rather than observed in a carrier.

nodes.description: Where TP53 is intact the accumulated damage triggers arrest and the RAD51D-null clone is removed. This branch is why RAD51D loss alone is not oncogenic, and it is the reason the order of hits matters: in fallopian tube organoids, RAD51D deletion alone impaired homologous recombination and arrested the cell, while concurrent TP53 deletion rescued the proliferation, stemness, senescence and apoptosis defects.
